one_run_caveat: One CI run is one measurement; Shard 5 (99%) and Shard 8 (16%) were cancelled at the 45-minute timeout, so 3 cases on Shard 5 and 3,233 cases (85 unstarted files + 2 partial files) on Shard 8 were not measured in this run.
answer: On this one run's evidence (and one run is one measurement), adding only the measured native test file durations to `utils/ci_test_durations.json` does NOT fit the 45-minute PR limit on 8 shards (or 9 shards), because `tests/test_generation_specificity_skill.py` on Shard 8 grew from its 1,148.699s weight to 5,918.248s (and `tests/test_d42_claude_d55.py` on Shard 5 grew from 2,184.783s to 3,352.067s): if only native weights are added, balanced_files predicts a largest scheduled shard of 7,518.450s (8 shards), 6,683.063s (9 shards), and 6,014.757s (10 shards), but packs ~6,370s of other files onto the `tests/test_generation_specificity_skill.py` shard for an actual measured load of 13,861.539s (57.76 ideal 4-worker min) at 8 shards, 12,062.054s (50.26 min) at 9 shards, and 10,756.118s (44.82 min) at 10 shards. If all 714 files measured in run 42976790438 (both native and non-native) are updated in the weights, the largest shard drops to 8,253.583s (34.39 ideal 4-worker min, ~37–38 min job wall) at 8 shards, 7,336.518s (30.57 min) at 9 shards, and 6,602.866s (27.51 min) at 10 shards (or 8,464.084s, 7,523.630s, and 6,771.267s when also imputing the 15 unrun Shard-8 native files at the 105.094s measured native mean) — meaning a full weight refresh (not native-only) can fit 45 minutes at 8 shards with ~6–7 min wall margin, while moving to 9 or 10 PR shards buys ~4–7 min of additional wall-clock headroom.
